newsitem.title: LATVIA: DEPOSITORY SAYS DVP WITH ESTONIA BY YEAR-END.
newsitem.headline: DEPOSITORY SAYS DVP WITH ESTONIA BY YEAR-END.

text.p: The central depository on Thursday said it will introduce the delivery versus payment (DVP) method for deals with Estonian and Latvian securities by the end of the year.

The agreement between the central depositories of the two countries, which comes into effect on July 1, allows Estonian public securities to be kept in accounts in the Latvian depository and vice versa.
The agreement allows any lisenced broker or bank to offer the service of selling Estonian securities in Latvia.
"The payment system will not be on the DVP level from the very start..it will not come sooner than the end of the year," Martinsh Rikshis, the president of the depository, told a news conference.
"We are at the moment concentrating more on introducing a real-time payment system in this country (for securities transactions) to replace the current three-day period," Rikshis said.
"By replacing T plus three formula by T plus zero we will make the big guarantee funds redundunt," Rikshis said.
The depository is participating in a central bank working group on the development of a communication system between the banks, Rikshis said.
When asked about Lithuania possiblly joining the depository agreement, Rikshis said that its market was not ready for that.
"It could be a matter of (avoiding increased) competition," Rikshis said.
